analysis.title: The Commodities Feed: Oil extends losses while copper gives back Nvidia bounce
key_insights: WTI stayed below $80/bbl on Tuesday as hopes of US-Iran talks unwound some geopolitical risk premium. Prices fell almost 4% on Monday to the lowest level since August.
Persian Gulf crude exports have stayed relatively resilient despite disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. Large US-Iran differences remain, so oil is vulnerable to any setback in talks.

Ukraine hit another major Russian refinery in the Perm region (over 260k b/d capacity). About 15 Russian refineries have been targeted since the start of November, over 3.6m b/d of nameplate capacity, more than half of Russia's total.
US natural gas fell more than 9% on Monday to about $3.1/MMBtu, the biggest daily drop since February. Milder weather forecasts and near-record US production should keep weighing on prices near term.
Copper gave back Monday's Nvidia-driven gains, falling more than 2% toward $12,000/t as focus returned to Chinese demand and US rates.

ING sees the copper weakness as a financial market story, not a fundamental deterioration. The Chinese physical market is tight, with elevated import premiums and nearby spreads signalling limited availability.
Copper previously accumulated in the US is starting to return to the international market, but this will take time to ease tightness elsewhere.

Aluminium's LME cash-to-three-month spread widened above $400/t on Monday as exchange availability sits at historical lows. Additional Indonesian supply is not yet largely deliverable against the LME.
ING expects macro concerns to keep copper volatile near term, while tight physical availability should limit downside.

sector_views.rationale: Risk premium is unwinding on US-Iran talk hopes, but large differences and Hormuz disruption leave oil vulnerable to talks failing.
Mild weather and record-level US production should weigh on prices near term.
Macro-driven volatility in copper is offset by tight physical markets in copper and aluminium.
